paper.title: Maths Higher Paper 2 (calculator): Mock 1
paper.instructions: You may use a calculator. Answer all the questions. Show your working: marks are given for method, and a correct answer with no working may not get full marks. If your calculator gives a long decimal, write down the full value before you round it. Diagrams are described in words; you can describe any diagram you would draw.

questions.topic: Ratio, Proportion and Rates of Change
questions.question_text:
A laptop costs £640.

In a sale, the price is reduced by 15%. After the sale, the sale price is increased by 15%.

Ali says, "The laptop is now back to £640."

Is Ali correct? You must show your working.

points: States Ali is not correct, with £625.60 (or 640 × 0.9775) as evidence
scheme.guidance: Accept a multiplier argument: 0.85 × 1.15 = 0.9775, which is not 1, for the first two marks. The final mark needs a clear conclusion. This question asks for working. A correct final answer with no working scores only the mark(s) for the answer itself, not the method marks. Award each method mark when that step is shown. If the working has a slip (e.g. a wrong number copied) but the final answer is correct, withhold only the mark(s) for the step that is wrong.

questions.topic: Ratio, Proportion and Rates of Change
questions.question_text:
Priya invests £4500 in a savings account.

The account pays 3.2% compound interest per year.

Work out the value of her investment at the end of 5 years. Give your answer to the nearest penny.

scheme.guidance: £720 interest (simple interest, giving £5220) scores 0. Accept £5267.578… for the method marks; the final mark needs £5267.58.

questions.topic: Ratio, Proportion and Rates of Change
questions.question_text:
Green paint is made by mixing blue paint and yellow paint in the ratio 3 : 5.

Kim has 1.2 litres of blue paint and 1.8 litres of yellow paint.

Work out the greatest amount of green paint Kim can make. Show your working.

points: Works out the blue needed for all the yellow (1.8 ÷ 5 × 3 = 1.08 litres) or the yellow needed for all the blue (1.2 ÷ 3 × 5 = 2 litres)
Identifies that the yellow paint runs out first (1.08 ≤ 1.2, or 2 > 1.8)
scheme.guidance: 3 litres (using all the paint) scores 0. 3.2 litres (using all the blue) scores 1 for the method. This question asks for working. A correct final answer with no working scores only the mark(s) for the answer itself, not the method marks. Award each method mark when that step is shown. If the working has a slip (e.g. a wrong number copied) but the final answer is correct, withhold only the mark(s) for the step that is wrong.

questions.topic: Ratio, Proportion and Rates of Change
questions.question_text:
A metal block is a cuboid measuring 4 cm by 5 cm by 12 cm.

The density of the metal is 8.9 g/cm³.

Work out the mass of the block in kilograms.

scheme.guidance: 2136 with no units, or in grams, scores 2.

questions.question_text:
The table gives information about the times, t minutes, that 40 people took to finish a puzzle.

| Time (t minutes) | Frequency |
|---|---|
| 0 < t ≤ 10 | 5 |
| 10 < t ≤ 20 | 12 |
| 20 < t ≤ 30 | 15 |
| 30 < t ≤ 40 | 8 |

Work out an estimate for the mean time. Show your working.

scheme.guidance: Using end points (10, 20, 30, 40) can score the second mark for dividing a consistent total by 40. Dividing by 4 scores at most 1. This question asks for working. A correct final answer with no working scores only the mark(s) for the answer itself, not the method marks. Award each method mark when that step is shown. If the working has a slip (e.g. a wrong number copied) but the final answer is correct, withhold only the mark(s) for the step that is wrong.

questions.question_text:
The mass of the Earth is 5.97 × 10²⁴ kg.

The mass of the Moon is 7.35 × 10²² kg.

How many times greater is the mass of the Earth than the mass of the Moon? Give your answer to 3 significant figures.

scheme.guidance: Accept 81.22… for the method mark; the answer mark needs 81.2.

questions.question_text:
ABC is a right-angled triangle.

Angle ABC = 90°. AB = 7.4 cm and BC = 11.2 cm.

Work out the size of angle ACB. Give your answer correct to 1 decimal place.

scheme.guidance: 56.5° (the angle at A) scores 2. A complete method via Pythagoras and sin or cos is fine.

questions.question_text:
A cylinder has radius 6 cm and height 15 cm. It is full of water.

All of the water is poured into an empty tank shaped like a cuboid. The base of the tank measures 20 cm by 15 cm.

Work out the depth of the water in the tank. Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures. Show your working.

points: Uses V = πr²h for the cylinder: π × 6² × 15
scheme.guidance: Using diameter 12 as the radius loses the first two marks but can score the third. This question asks for working. A correct final answer with no working scores only the mark(s) for the answer itself, not the method marks. Award each method mark when that step is shown. If the working has a slip (e.g. a wrong number copied) but the final answer is correct, withhold only the mark(s) for the step that is wrong.

questions.question_text:
A, B, C and D are points on a circle, so ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral.

Angle ABC = (3x + 10)° and angle ADC = (2x + 20)°.

Work out the size of angle ABC. Give a reason for each stage of your working.

points: Reason: opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add up to 180°
scheme.guidance: The reason mark needs the words 'cyclic quadrilateral' (or equivalent) and 'opposite'.

questions.topic: Ratio, Proportion and Rates of Change
questions.question_text:
y is inversely proportional to the square of x.

When x = 5, y = 12.

Work out the value of y when x = 8.

scheme.guidance: y = k/x (k = 60, y = 7.5) scores 0.

questions.question_text:
A bag contains 5 red counters and 3 blue counters.

Zac takes a counter at random and does not replace it. He then takes a second counter at random.

Work out the probability that the two counters are different colours. Show your working.

points: Uses the second-pick probabilities out of 7: 5/8 × 3/7 or 3/8 × 5/7
scheme.guidance: With replacement (2 × 5/8 × 3/8 = 30/64) scores 1. Accept 0.536 (3 sf). This question asks for working. A correct final answer with no working scores only the mark(s) for the answer itself, not the method marks. Award each method mark when that step is shown. If the working has a slip (e.g. a wrong number copied) but the final answer is correct, withhold only the mark(s) for the step that is wrong.

questions.question_text:
Here are the first five terms of a quadratic sequence.

4   11   22   37   56

Find an expression, in terms of n, for the nth term of the sequence.

points: Second difference is 4, so the sequence starts 2n²
scheme.guidance: 4n² with a correct method for the rest scores 1.

questions.question_text:
Line L passes through the points (2, 5) and (6, −3).

Find the equation of the line that is perpendicular to L and passes through the point (4, 1).

scheme.guidance: Accept any equivalent form, e.g. 2y = x − 2 or x − 2y − 2 = 0.

questions.question_text:
Make x the subject of the formula

y = (3x + 2) / (x − 4)

points: Collects x terms on one side and factorises: x(y − 3) = 2 + 4y
scheme.guidance: Accept equivalent forms such as x = (−4y − 2)/(3 − y).

questions.question_text:
Solve 3x² − 7x − 4 = 0

Give your solutions correct to 2 decimal places.

points: Substitutes correctly into the quadratic formula: x = (7 ± √(49 + 48)) ÷ 6
scheme.guidance: One correct solution scores 2. Completing the square is fine.

questions.question_text:
A cyclist rides 250 m, correct to the nearest 10 m.

The time taken is 32.4 seconds, correct to 1 decimal place.

Work out the upper bound for the cyclist's average speed. Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures. Show your working.

points: Uses the bounds 255 m and 32.35 s
scheme.guidance: Using 32.45 s (giving 7.86) scores 1 for the distance bound. This question asks for working. A correct final answer with no working scores only the mark(s) for the answer itself, not the method marks. Award each method mark when that step is shown. If the working has a slip (e.g. a wrong number copied) but the final answer is correct, withhold only the mark(s) for the step that is wrong.

questions.topic: Ratio, Proportion and Rates of Change
questions.question_text:
The number of bacteria, P, in a dish t hours after a test starts is

P = 500 × 1.08ᵗ

(a) Work out the number of bacteria after 6 hours.

(b) Work out after how many whole hours the number of bacteria first goes above 2000.

points: (b) Tries values of t either side, e.g. t = 18 gives 1998 and t = 19 gives 2157.8…
scheme.guidance: In (b), 18 hours scores 1 if 1998 is seen. Using logarithms is fine.

questions.subtopic: Sine rule, cosine rule and area of a triangle
questions.question_text:
In triangle PQR, PQ = 8.5 cm, PR = 12.3 cm and angle QPR = 47°.

(a) Work out the length of QR. Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

(b) Work out the area of triangle PQR. Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

scheme.guidance: Calculator in radians gives a wrong value: award method marks only.

questions.question_text:
There are 60 students in a year group.

35 study French, 28 study Spanish and 9 study neither language.

One of the students who studies French is chosen at random.

Work out the probability that this student also studies Spanish. Show your working.

points: Works out that 60 − 9 = 51 study at least one language
scheme.guidance: 12/60 (or 1/5) scores 2. A correct Venn diagram with 23, 12, 16, 9 scores the first two marks. This question asks for working. A correct final answer with no working scores only the mark(s) for the answer itself, not the method marks. Award each method mark when that step is shown. If the working has a slip (e.g. a wrong number copied) but the final answer is correct, withhold only the mark(s) for the step that is wrong.

questions.question_text:
Two bottles are mathematically similar.

The smaller bottle has height 12 cm and volume 320 cm³.

The larger bottle has height 18 cm.

Work out the volume of the larger bottle.

scheme.guidance: 480 cm³ (linear scale factor used) scores 1. 720 cm³ (area scale factor) scores 1.

questions.question_text:
The table gives information about the heights, h cm, of 100 plants.

| Height (h cm) | Frequency |
|---|---|
| 0 < h ≤ 20 | 16 |
| 20 < h ≤ 30 | 22 |
| 30 < h ≤ 40 | 30 |
| 40 < h ≤ 60 | 24 |
| 60 < h ≤ 100 | 8 |

A histogram is drawn for this data. Use the frequency densities to work out an estimate for the number of plants with a height between 45 cm and 70 cm.

points: Frequency densities for the two classes used: 24 ÷ 20 = 1.2 and 8 ÷ 40 = 0.2
Uses the parts of the classes: 15 × 1.2 = 18 and 10 × 0.2 = 2
scheme.guidance: Proportion method (15/20 × 24 + 10/40 × 8) is fine for full marks.

questions.question_text:
Solve the simultaneous equations

y = x² − 3x + 1
y = 2x − 3

Show your working.

scheme.guidance: The last mark needs both pairs, correctly paired. This question asks for working. A correct final answer with no working scores only the mark(s) for the answer itself, not the method marks. Award each method mark when that step is shown. If the working has a slip (e.g. a wrong number copied) but the final answer is correct, withhold only the mark(s) for the step that is wrong.

questions.question_text:
(a) Show that the equation x³ + 4x − 7 = 0 has a solution between x = 1 and x = 2.

(b) Using the iteration formula

xₙ₊₁ = ∛(7 − 4xₙ)

with x₀ = 1.2, find the values of x₁, x₂ and x₃. Give your answers correct to 4 decimal places.

points: (a) Substitutes both values: x = 1 gives −2 and x = 2 gives 9
(a) States there is a change of sign, so there is a solution between 1 and 2
scheme.guidance: In (b), allow error carried forward from a wrong x₁ for x₂ and x₃ if the formula is used correctly.

questions.question_text:
OAB is a sector of a circle with centre O and radius 9 cm. Angle AOB = 70°.

The chord AB is drawn. The segment is the region between the chord AB and the arc AB.

Work out the area of the segment. Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures. Show your working.

points: Area of triangle OAB = ½ × 9 × 9 × sin 70° = 38.05…
scheme.guidance: Accept 11.42… for the method marks. This question asks for working. A correct final answer with no working scores only the mark(s) for the answer itself, not the method marks. Award each method mark when that step is shown. If the working has a slip (e.g. a wrong number copied) but the final answer is correct, withhold only the mark(s) for the step that is wrong.
